account.note: The identity-only shape. Every entitlement field is ABSENT because no lookup happened - not null, not defaulted, absent.
email is optional and display-only; its presence does not make the answer a lookup.
A live grant. entitlement_stale is false BECAUSE a lookup happened and was fresh.
The website's outage fallback, reported honestly: cache + stale, with the age visible to the user.
No plan. A 200 here and a typed 402 only when it stops paid work.
plan_id is present on a REFUSAL: a lapsed Pro subscription is still Pro. Only `granted` REQUIRES a plan; no access value forbids one.
subject_hash is exactly 16 lowercase hex characters on this authenticated route.
`unverified` means nothing was asked, so it cannot report an answer.
Access to something unnamed cannot later be attributed or capped.
A lookup that happened has a time it happened at. The backend must not fabricate one, so it must not omit one either.
No offset. The client would read it in whatever zone it assumes, silently shifting how fresh a billing answer looks.
A live provider check cannot be stale.
A cache-sourced refusal is never authoritative. The entitlement client refuses this body upstream, so the route cannot build it - the response model mirrors the rule so both layers agree.

entitlement.note: The outage fallback, 18 hours old and well inside the cached-grant bound.
Exactly 86400 + 300 seconds before the reference instant. Bounds are INCLUSIVE, so the website's published maximum is usable at the value it publishes.
The real website shape for a lapsed subscription: it names the plan.
THE row that matters. A stale negative must never become a 402 telling a paying customer to buy a second plan during an outage.
An hour old and claiming to be live. Accepted under the single day-long limit this table replaced.
Two days old. An expired stale positive is a DEPENDENCY failure, never a missing subscription.
